common_name: Snow Muffin Loropetalum (Dwarf Mounding White-Flowered Green Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade; Snow Muffin's tight, rounded mound and clean green foliage suit foundation plantings and small-space borders better than the larger, burgundy-leaved loropetalum selections.

directions: US Plant Patent 11,766 covers Snow Muffin, a dwarf, dense-mounding loropetalum that keeps the species' all-green foliage rather than the burgundy tones common to most named selections. New growth emerges light green and matures to a deeper olive shade, setting off the flossy white spring flower clusters that repeat sporadically into early summer. Its tidy, rounded habit needs little corrective pruning, making it a low-maintenance choice for small beds, mixed borders, or mass plantings where a compact green backdrop is wanted. Established plants tolerate short dry spells but perform best with regular moisture and acidic, well-drained soil.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Gardening Solutions

common_name: Jazz Hands White Loropetalum (Dark-Green Reblooming White Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in part to full sun; Jazz Hands White (sold under this trade name) pairs the compact habit of the Jazz Hands series with clean, dark-green foliage and heavy white bloom rather than the purple leaves typical of most series members.

directions: Registered as 'Hakuou' under US Plant Patent 27,751, Jazz Hands White is the green-leaved, white-flowered member of the Proven Winners Jazz Hands loropetalum series. Its rich dark-green evergreen foliage stays glossy through the season and provides strong contrast for the large, pure-white, fringe-petaled flower clusters that open heavily in spring and continue in lighter flushes through summer. The rounded, mounded growth habit fits foundation plantings, mixed borders, or mass plantings where a lighter, more traditional look is wanted alongside purple-leaved loropetalum cultivars. Light shearing right after the main spring bloom maintains a dense form without sacrificing later flowering.

common_name: Jazz Hands Velvet Loropetalum (Heat-Tolerant Burgundy-Leaf Pink Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in part to full sun; Jazz Hands Velvet (sold under this trade name) holds its rich burgundy leaf color best with several hours of direct sun and performs reliably through hot, humid Gulf South summers.

directions: Registered as 'Gekkou' under US Plant Patent 29,320, Jazz Hands Velvet is a compact, mounded loropetalum bred for heat tolerance within the Proven Winners Jazz Hands series. Its rich burgundy-purple foliage holds color well into summer heat rather than fading, and contrasts with clusters of bright pink, spidery, fringe-petaled flowers concentrated in spring with lighter rebloom later on. The dense, rounded habit suits it to specimen planting, mixed borders, or informal low hedges in warm-climate landscapes. It tolerates brief drought once established but colors and flowers best with consistent moisture and a spring feeding.
